newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent up on API data, but Iraq spurs bears.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent up on API data, but Iraq spurs bears.

text.p: September Brent futures rose on Wednesday in Asia -- but earlier highs were pared -- following bullish overnight data from the American Petroleum Institute (API).
But brokers said news that Iraq denied it had asked the United Nations to delay the start of the resumption of oil sales, would reignite worries of a flood of Iraqi oil hitting the market in August.
September Brent crude futures on SIMEX were last traded at $18.78 per barrel, 19 cents higher than London's overnight settlement but off the intraday high of $18.85.
September NYMEX crude futures, on ACCESS, were last traded at $20.08, up 23 cents from New York after trading 3,700 lots in the after-hours trade.
Brokers attributed the gain to API data.
The crude draw of 9.7 million barrels compared with expectations of a draw of 2.00 million and reflected the effect of Hurricane Danny, analysts said.
However, a fall in refinery utilisation and gasoline production undermined the strength of the crude data, traders said in New York earlier.
But gasoline stocks fell 3.17 million barrels, higher than the expectations of 1.7 million barrels, although implied demand was falling.
That sparked a further rally in August gasoline, which expires on Thursday.
The contract rose in New York 1.63 cent per gallon to last trade at 66.47, but then added 0.93 to last trade at 67.40 on ACCESS.

But Iraq offered the market a bearish signal as Iraqi newspapers Wednesday quoted a foreign ministry spokesman saying reports Iraq had asked for the second oil-for-aid programme to be delayed were baseless.
Iraq has not exported any oil after the first programme ceased early in June. Iraq is permitted to sell $2 billion worth of oil every six months.
In theory, Baghdad has until the end of the first week of September to sell $1 billion worth of oil under the second programme.
